title: SpikeStereoNet: A Brain-Inspired Framework for Stereo Depth Estimation from Spike Streams
claim: Train on synthetic data produced by a simulation pipeline, then transfer the pre-trained model to real-world data collected with a physical sensor rig.
layout: 2 stacked horizontal bands (synthetic top, real bottom), left-to-right flow with arrows, a vertical transfer arrow linking the model bars on the right
description: The figure has two horizontal bands. The top band has a cream background and covers synthetic training. Boxes for Scene, Object and Sensor feed the Blender logo through function modules and a sampling process. Blender outputs an image and a depth map, which sit in a box with the depth map outlined in red dashes. A spiking simulator and video frame interpolation produce a spike stream. The depth map supervises training and the spike stream is the input, and both feed a pair of yellow bars that stand for the network. The bottom band has a light blue background and covers real data. It runs from a photo of real-world scenes through a stereo rig (spike cameras plus a Kinect) to a real dataset of spike volume and depth. A blue pair of bars is fine-tuned. A large yellow arrow labelled Transfer links the two model bars. Black arrows and bold stage titles guide the eye left to right.
caption: The overall pipeline is illustrated in the figure below. The upper path represents the training and evaluation process on synthetic dataset, while the lower path shows the transfer learning and testing procedure on real spike stream data by using the pre-trained model.
abstract: Conventional frame-based cameras often struggle with stereo depth estimation in rapidly changing scenes. In contrast, bio-inspired spike cameras emit asynchronous events at microsecond-level resolution, providing an alternative sensing modality. However, existing methods lack specialized stereo algorithms and benchmarks tailored to the spike data. To address this gap, we propose SpikeStereoNet, a brain-inspired framework and the first to estimate stereo depth directly from raw spike streams. The model fuses raw spike streams from two viewpoints and iteratively refines depth estimation through a recurrent spiking neural network (RSNN) update module. To benchmark our approach, we introduce a large-scale synthetic spike stream dataset and a real-world stereo spike dataset with dense depth annotations. SpikeStereoNet outperforms existing methods on both datasets by leveraging spike streams' ability to capture subtle edges and intensity shifts in challenging regions such as textureless surfaces and extreme lighting conditions. Furthermore, our framework exhibits strong data efficiency, maintaining high accuracy even with substantially reduced training data. The source code and datasets will be publicly available.
